title: Introduce finalization-fence and resilient reconnect playbook to prevent missing trailing tokens on Hosted SSE
creator: Priya Kaur
description: High-severity customer reports showed truncation of final token(s) when a Hosted SSE stream experienced a disconnect during high-concurrency flush windows. This ticket defines a corrective implementation ("finalization-fence"), an operational reconnect playbook, and deployment/upgrade guidance for Dedicated and Private customers.
repro_steps: 1) Start a high-throughput text-generation job via Hosted API with streaming enabled and long tail token output (>= 300 tokens).
2) Simultaneously trigger rapid connection churn by simulating intermittent reverse-proxy 499 closes from the client side while backend worker is in the final 'flush and seal' phase,
3) Observe clients reporting that the SSE stream ended without the expected final punctuation or final message that indicates logical completion,
4) Capture server-side trace for request id and observe worker log showing 'flush initiated' but no 'final-sealed' marker.
telemetry_summary: Over a 72-hour window we saw ~0.12% of streaming requests for tier-hosted customers hit missing-final-token symptoms under sustained 95th percentile load. Traces correlated with worker pod restarts or proxy-initiated connection termination within the 40-80ms window after the kernel-level write returned 0 bytes written. Edge logs show client-initiated closes (499) in ~72% of cases; remaining cases were internal eviction/restart.
root_cause: Race between the runtime's in-memory flush path and the network connection closure. When a worker entered its final KV/cache commit and output drain, there was no durable, client-observable finalization message persisted outside the in-memory stream buffer. If the connection was closed by the edge or the worker was preempted before the final flush was acknowledged on the socket, clients saw an abrupt end without a deterministic final marker. Two contributing factors: (1) the runtime's graceful shutdown flow assumed best-effort socket writes would complete before process eviction, and (2) the edge's early-close behavior (499) frequently cut the socket before kernel buffers drained under high load.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Temporarily increase worker graceful-shutdown timeout for Hosted to 1.5s where possible. 2) Enable conservative connection draining at the edge for high-throughput model routes. 3) Support team to add customer-facing guidance to increase client reconnect window for streaming consumers and to enable delta-replay logic client-side.
fix_description: Implement a 'finalization-fence' event persisted to the streaming checkpoint store before the final token flush completes. The fence is a small, idempotent event (2-4 bytes metadata) stored atomically with the request's final state. When a worker is interrupted mid-flush, a reconnecting client can request 'resume-to-fence' which returns the latest sealed chunk and a deterministic boolean indicating completion. The server will also emit a 'closing-signal' SSE event prior to beginning the final flush when possible, allowing proxies and clients to observe imminent finalization and adjust timeouts. This approach decouples correctness (final token delivered) from the timing of socket writes and guards against worker preemption and edge early-close semantics.
implementation_notes:
- Add 'fence' write path in runtime: lightweight atomic write to checkpoint store (already exists for snapshots) with idempotent semantics.
- Expose new SSE event type: event: finalization-fence
- Add resume endpoint: /v1/resume?request_id=<id>&to_fence=true returning last sealed chunk and fence state.
- Adjust worker shutdown sequence: emit closing-signal -> write fence -> attempt flush -> signal 'final-sealed' (best-effort). If flush fails, fence allows clients to detect completed output without socket data.
- Add feature flag (runtime.fence.enabled) for staged rollout.
- Ensure encryption and ACL model of checkpoint store is unchanged; no plaintext model outputs persisted beyond existing snapshot rules.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind runtime.fence.enabled flag, default off (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219).
2) Canary 1% of Hosted traffic in us-west with flag on and enhanced telemetry (03/16),
3) Expand to 25% after 24h if no regressions observed, monitor SLOs and token-per-request cost delta,
4) Full rollout for Hosted after 72h stable canary and stakeholder signoff,
5) For Dedicated customers: deliver a configuration bundle and migration notes; enable opt-in for operators via runtime flag and offer an assisted migration runbook,
6) For Private customers: include as part of 2026.04 Private runtime patch; document upgrade steps, database migrations (none required), and configuration toggle.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fence write/read idempotence and error paths,
Integration tests simulating socket early-close during final flush and asserting resume-to-fence returns finalized state,
Chaos test: kill worker during final flush under 50k RPS load in staging, assert client-visible finalization via resume endpoint,
Benchmark: measure latency/CPU/TX change for typical streaming workload (expected <1.2% CPU overhead),
E2E canary with synthetic clients that artificially drop connections and attempt resume for 48h
runbook_for_support:
- When customer reports truncated final token: capture request_id, timestamp, and client-side socket logs.
- Query streaming-checkpoint for fence state: /internal/checkpoint/<request_id>. If fence present and sealed=true, advise client to call /v1/resume?request_id=<id>&to_fence=true; return sealed chunk and final marker.
- If fence absent and worker logs show 'shutdown during flush', escalate to oncall infra (priority P0).
- If edge shows 499 spikes, coordinate with Edge team to enable conservative draining for affected routes.
customer_escalations: Case #RD-2311: enterprise-corp reported repeated mid-stream truncation during nightly batch QPS spikes; provided logs and confirmed fix in canary stage.
Case #RD-2324: fintech-client reported missing final punctuation leading to failed downstream parsers; temporary mitigation applied (edge-drain) and customer notified.
next_steps: Finalize PR addressing code review comments by 2026-03-16,
Coordinate with Edge team to apply temporary drain policy for high-throughput routes,
Schedule Dedicated/Private customer advisory and opt-in migration window,
Add automated alerting rule: streaming.resume-failures > 5m -> paging oncall
notes: This change aims to make final token delivery deterministic even under aggressive preemption or edge early-close semantics. Because it introduces a small persisted artifact per request, we validated storage cost impact and found it negligible given retention policies. Keep an eye on token-per-request egress metrics during the canary.
